summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM-powered applications move into production at scale, where unmonitored prompts, workflows, and model calls can lead to runaway costs, undetected hallucinations, and degraded user experiences. These tools let teams trace workflows, evaluate outputs, track per-model spend, and connect AI-specific issues to broader application performance. With New Relic reporting 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring adoption, choosing the right tool depends on your stack, budget, and preference for open-source versus managed solutions.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Prompts, traces, workflows, chains, agent steps, and evaluation metrics—deeply integrated with the LangChain ecosystem.
features: Rich debugging and step-by-step trace visualization
Built-in evaluation and testing framework (LLM-as-judge, datasets)
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month; overage ~$2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention. Commonly cited around £80/month for higher-volume usage.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph that need the richest debugging and evaluation tooling.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests, token usage, latency, and cost across 300+ models via a lightweight proxy/gateway.
features: One-line base-URL change for integration (setup in minutes)
Cost tracking computed across 300+ models using a model-cost repository
tools.pricing: Free at 10,000 requests/month; Growth/Pro at $20/month (100K requests); ~£20/month equivalent; Pro reaches 100K traces around $79/month. Enterprise custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting the cheapest, simplest setup for cost tracking and quick spend governance across multiple model providers.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, model experiments, evaluations, and end-to-end ML/AI pipeline performance.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans with consumption/seat-based pricing (custom for enterprise).
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams needing unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Model performance, embeddings, drift, RAG quality, and LLM traces with strong evaluation focus.
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize managed platform offers free tier and enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams needing standards-based (OpenTelemetry) evaluation and drift monitoring for RAG and production models.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Prompts, traces, spans, cost, latency, and online evaluations—available both as cloud and self-hosted.
tools.pricing: Cloud free for <50K events, then ~£20 for 500K; Self-hosted ~£30/month infra plus ~2 hours/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Cost-conscious teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with a generous free tier.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, and metrics using OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation for vendor-neutral telemetry.
features: Exports to any OTel-compatible backend (Datadog, New Relic, etc.)
Automatic instrumentation of popular LLM SDKs
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs limited to your chosen observability backend's charges.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral LLM telemetry that plugs into existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy like Helicone to get per-user and per-model cost visibility, then cache repeated or identical requests to avoid paying for duplicate completions.
Route tasks to the cheapest capable model—use smaller or distilled models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, applying prompt routing or tiered fallbacks.
Trim token usage by compressing prompts, limiting context window size, truncating retrieved RAG chunks, and setting sensible max_output_token limits.
Set budgets, alerts, and rate limits per department or user, and continuously monitor traces to catch runaway loops, retries, or inefficient agent chains before they inflate spend.
